description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a comforting and nutritious staple, beloved across the Middle East for its simplicity and rich flavor. This hearty soup features earthy red lentils simmered with aromatic vegetables and brightened with a squeeze of fresh lemon, creating a truly soul-warming experience. It's an ideal meal for any day, offering both warmth and a taste of authentic regional cuisine.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Chop the onion, mince the garlic, and dice the carrot and potato into small, even pieces. This ensures everything cooks uniformly.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Vegetables and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the diced carrot and potato, and cook for about 3-4 minutes, allowing them to slightly soften. Add the ground cumin and turmeric (if using) and cook for another minute, stirring constantly to toast the spices and release their aroma.

instructions.title: Combine Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, then pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend and Season
instructions.text: Once cooked, you can leave the soup as is for a rustic texture, or use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup to your desired consistency. If you do not have an immersion blender, carefully transfer about half of the soup to a regular blender, blend, and return to the pot. Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the dried mint and fresh lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference. Ladle the hot soup into bowls and garnish with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro before serving immediately.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a pinch of red pepper flakes with the spices for a subtle kick, or a dash of sumac at the end for tang.
Do not overcook the lentils; they should be tender but not mushy unless you prefer a completely smooth soup. Rinsing them well prevents cloudiness.
Adas soup is excellent leftover. It tends to thicken in the refrigerator, so you may need to add a splash of water or broth when reheating to achieve the desired consistency.
